# Issue 2: Splitting a damage charge two ways loses a cent

## Outcome

When a damage charge is shared between borrowers, every cent of it is billed to someone. The shares
add up exactly to the charge. D-301 (£33.33, two borrowers) bills £16.67 and £16.66, totalling £33.33.

## Requirements

- The system shall return shares from `splitCharge` that add up exactly to the charge, for any whole-cent charge and any number of ways.
- When a charge does not divide evenly, the system shall give each of the first `remainder` borrowers one extra cent, where remainder is the charge in cents modulo the number of ways.
- The system shall keep every pair of shares within one cent of each other.
- When a charge divides evenly, the system shall give every borrower the same share.
- The system shall return as many shares as there are ways, as integer cents.
- If the charge is negative or not a whole number of cents, or ways is less than 1 or not a whole number, the system shall refuse the split with an error.

## Must not change

- Amounts stay integer cents; no floats are used for money.
- Even charges split into equal shares as before, and one borrower still pays the whole charge.
- Negative charges are still refused.
- `src/auth/` is untouched.
- The `bun run desk split` output format stays the same.

## Out of scope

- Weighted or percentage splits.
- Changing which borrower gets the extra cent per charge (the first borrowers in the listed order always do).
- Any change to late fees, reservations, borrowing rules or member search.

## Done when

- The new tests in `tests/fees/split.test.ts` pass, and the existing tests still pass.
- `bun run desk split D-301` shows shares that add up to £33.33.
- `bun run gate` exits 0.

content.text:
`splitCharge` now hands the leftover cents to the first borrowers, one extra cent each. D-301 (£33.33, two borrowers) therefore splits into £16.67 and £16.66, which adds up to £33.33.

The change is in `src/fees/split.ts`. Each borrower gets the charge divided by the number of ways, rounded down. The first `remainder` borrowers then get one more cent, where `remainder` is the charge in cents modulo the number of ways. The existing checks that refuse bad input are untouched, and `src/auth/` wasn't touched.

`bun run gate` passed on its own, with 16 tests. I didn't run `bun run desk split D-301` directly, so the CLI output is covered only by the gate.
